question_stem:
A spring hangs vertically from a point P, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
A mass M is attached to the lower end of the spring. The reading x from the metre rule is taken, as
shown in Fig. 4.1. Fig. 4.2 shows the relationship between x and M.
question_stem_latex:
A spring hangs vertically from a point P, as shown in Fig. 4.1.
A mass M is attached to the lower end of the spring. The reading x from the metre rule is taken, as
shown in Fig. 4.1. Fig. 4.2 shows the relationship between x and M.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question_text:
Explain how the apparatus in Fig. 4.1 may be used to determine the load on the spring at the
elastic limit.
parts.question_text_latex:
Explain how the apparatus in Fig. 4.1 may be used to determine the load on the spring at the
elastic limit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text: State and explain whether Fig. 4.2 suggests that the spring obeys Hooke’s law.
parts.question_text_latex: State and explain whether Fig. 4.2 suggests that the spring obeys Hooke’s law.

parts.label: (c)
parts.question_text:
Use Fig. 4.2 to determine the spring constant, in N m^{-1}, of the spring.
spring constant = N m^{-1}

Use Fig. 4.2 to determine the spring constant, in N $m^{-1}$, of the spring.
$spring constant = N m^{-1} $
